newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO sees boost from accounting move.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO sees boost from accounting move.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV said on Tuesday that total risk provisioning would fall and earnings and dividends would rise as a result of the decision of Dutch banks to reveal their hidden reserves (VAR).
Director-general of planning and control Wilco ten Berg told a media briefing on the accounting change that this assumed no changes in other factors affecting the bank.

However, he declined to reveal the size of the bank's VAR, estimated by analysts at between 3.0 billion and 4.0 billion guilders at January 1, saying it would be announced for the first time with the bank's 1996 results on February 27.

Banking is the only sector in the Netherlands allowed to create hidden reserves but Dutch banks are revealing them for the first time in 1997 ahead of changes to banking law which would have required them to do so anyway.
The reserves show that the banks have provided more for bad loans in the past than actual losses.
Ten Berg said ABN AMRO would transfer part of the the VAR, or provision for general risks, to shareholders' equity and part to the FAR, a new fund for general contingencies.
He said it would also show, for the first half of 1997, the actual loan losses and changes to the FAR as separate items.
The precise level of loan losses has never been revealed in the past.
Ten Berg said total risk provisions each year would fall because the new FAR fund would be smaller than the old VAR reserve.
"That means that earnings, everything else being equal, will go up," he told the briefing.
He also confirmed that ABN AMRO would maintain its dividend pay-out ratio on the higher earnings per share, lifting dividends per share.
